html:
SMTO-MEM-0009 — SMTO couldn't open its saved memories

GUID: 6c1e2321-124e-4268-86c7-98821e972de8
Slug: memory-unavailable
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't read or write the file where memories are kept, so this memory action didn't happen. Your saved memories weren't changed by this error.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the computer running the SMTO server has free disk space, and free some up if it's nearly full. SMTO can't create or update the memory file when the disk is full.
  2. Make sure only one copy of SMTO is using this data: stop any other SMTO window or installed app, then start SMTO again. Another copy can keep the memory file busy, so this copy can't open it in time.
  3. Open the Memory Editor and select Refresh to see whether your memories load, then repeat the action. If the list loads, SMTO can read the memory file again and the action can work.

What success looks like

  • The Memory Editor lists your memories, and the action you tried now completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO; the memory file may be damaged or its folder permissions may have changed. Don't delete or move the memory file (agent_memory.db) in SMTO's data folder; it holds all your saved memories.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Memory storage was unavailable: creating or opening agent_memory.db failed (OSError or sqlite3.Error), a stored record could not be decoded, or the Memory capability had no bound store.

What this means

  • Memory initialization/connection/status encounters storage errors, a stored record cannot be decoded, or the capability has no usable store instance. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • Memory initialization/connection/status encounters storage errors, a stored record cannot be decoded, or the capability has no usable store instance.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish service initialization, storage access and malformed retained data using the bounded diagnostic.

How to fix it

  • Inspect agent_memory.db beside the run database in the state directory (AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR): check free disk space, file ownership and permissions, other processes holding locks (30-second busy timeout) and integrity (run PRAGMA integrity_check on a copy). Restore access without deleting existing data; if MemoryCapability.execute raised it, confirm the runtime context supplies _memory_store or _memory_store_path.
  • Inspect controller state storage availability and the safe diagnostic. Restore the supported storage path; preserve existing data.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported storage access is restored with existing data preserved and the intended record can be read.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
